correctness.rationale: For the centrally symmetric cuboctahedron \(K=[-1,1]^3\cap\{\|x\|_1\le2\}\), the standard boundary-cover lemma reduces a six-blocker construction to three finite checks: the six half-scaled centers lie on \(\partial K\), their pairwise differences avoid \(\operatorname{int}K\), and their translates of \(\operatorname{int}K\) cover \(\partial K\). The first two are immediate exact inequalities. The third is strengthened to a cover by the closed inset with clearance \(1/13\) and certified facet-by-facet by exact rational polygon clipping. The actual packaged verifier was replayed successfully and uses no floating point or sampling.

value.rationale: Blocking number is a named convex-geometric invariant with an explicit open-problem history. The regular cuboctahedron is a canonical centrally symmetric Archimedean solid, and a six-blocker construction reaches the conjectured dimension-three lower value without assuming that conjecture. The positive rational clearance \(1/13\) makes the construction robust and exactly reproducible, so the result provides a useful benchmark for future lower-bound or classification work rather than a routine numerical example.
